```{r, include = FALSE}
# The chunks run only in a build with the core's `experimental` feature.
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>",
                      eval = thiessen::core_experimental())
```

`xaddivortes()` fits the AddiVortes model, a sum of Voronoi tessellations,
under a compute budget instead of by Markov chain Monte Carlo. The columns
are scored by mutual information with the response, the tessellations are
built in turn on the running residual, and rounds replace the least useful
share and refit the rest while the budget lasts. The fit has two uses: a
fast point estimate, and the starting state of the exact sampler, which
changes where the chains start and not the posterior they target. Both are
experimental.

## A fast fit

Friedman's first function, five relevant covariates among ten:

```{r}
library(thiessen)
set.seed(1)
friedman <- function(n) {
  x <- matrix(runif(10 * n), n, 10)
  f <- 10 * sin(pi * x[, 1] * x[, 2]) + 20 * (x[, 3] - 0.5)^2 +
    10 * x[, 4] + 5 * x[, 5]
  list(x = x, y = f + rnorm(n), f = f)
}
train <- friedman(300)
test <- friedman(300)
fit <- xaddivortes(train$x, train$y, seed = 1)
fit
sqrt(mean((predict(fit, test$x) - test$f)^2))
```

The budget is in approximate sweeps of the exact sampler on the same data
(default 50); `xaddivortes_params()` holds every setting and its default.

```{r}
round(sort(fit$fast$column_scores, decreasing = TRUE), 3)
```

## Intervals

`sigma(fit)` is the in-sample residual root mean square. It understates the
noise when the fit overfits, most on small data, so the intervals of
`predict(fit, interval = "prediction")` are a rough guide. A split-conformal
interval (Lei and others, 2018) is calibrated without that assumption: fit
on one part of the data and widen the prediction by a quantile of the
absolute residuals on the other.

```{r}
half <- sample(nrow(train$x), nrow(train$x) / 2)
proper <- xaddivortes(train$x[half, ], train$y[half], seed = 1)
residuals <- abs(train$y[-half] - predict(proper, train$x[-half, ]))
k <- ceiling(0.95 * (length(residuals) + 1))
width <- sort(residuals)[k]
y_test <- test$f + rnorm(nrow(test$x))
mean(abs(y_test - predict(proper, test$x)) <= width)
```

## Warm starts

`thiessen(start = "fast")` starts every chain from its own fast fit, after
which the configured burn-in and draws run:

```{r}
control <- thiessen_control(
  general_params = general_params(burn_in = 50, draws = 100)
)
warm <- suppressWarnings(
  thiessen(train$x, train$y, control, seed = 1, chains = 2, start = "fast")
)
sqrt(mean((predict(warm, test$x) - test$f)^2))
```

## References

Lei, J., G'Sell, M., Rinaldo, A., Tibshirani, R. J. and Wasserman, L.
(2018). Distribution-free predictive inference for regression. Journal of
the American Statistical Association 113(523), 1094-1111.
